This script runs a principal component analysis (PCA) of the seven log antibody levels, then asks whether the principal components predict cryptococcosis status. The correlation plots and PCA plots are drawn in [Figures](figures.qmd), and the eigenvalue table in [Tables](tables.qmd).

## Why PCA

The antibody levels are correlated with one another, most strongly GXM-IgM with Lam-IgM (see the correlation plots in [Figures](figures.qmd)), which makes their individual coefficients in a joint regression model unstable. PCA was used to account for this correlation [@yoon2022antibody]: it re-expresses the seven measurements as seven uncorrelated components. The first component, PC1, acts as a summary score of overall antibody level. It runs opposite to the antibodies, so a higher PC1 means lower antibody levels.

## Fit the PCA

PCA is run on the log antibody levels of participants with complete antibody data. `scale = TRUE` standardizes each antibody first, so that no single antibody dominates because of its units.

## Do the components predict cryptococcosis?

A logistic regression of cryptococcosis status on all seven components. Because all seven are included, the model as a whole fits exactly as well as one using the seven log antibodies directly; the difference is that each component's coefficient can be read separately. The question of interest is whether the summary score, PC1, is associated with case status.
